title: Spiral Matrix
description:
# Spiral Matrix

Read a matrix and print all of its elements in **spiral order**: start at the top-left, go right across the top row, then down the right side, along the bottom, up the left side, and spiral inward until every element has been visited.

## Input

- Line 1: two integers `R` and `C` - rows and columns.
- Next `R` lines: each contains `C` space-separated integers.

## Output

All elements in spiral order, space-separated on a single line.

```
Input:
3 3
1 2 3
4 5 6
7 8 9

Output:
1 2 3 6 9 8 7 4 5
```

## Think about

- Track four boundaries - top, bottom, left, right - and peel off one layer at a time, shrinking the boundaries after each edge. Be careful not to re-visit a row or column when the remaining area is a single line.
starterCode:
r, c = map(int, input().split())
matrix = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(r)]

# TODO: print all elements in clockwise spiral order, space-separated
hints: Peel off one edge at a time - top row, right column, bottom row, left column - spiralling inward.
Track four boundaries (top, bottom, left, right). Walk the top row then `top += 1`, the right column then `right -= 1`, and so on, guarding against a single remaining row or column.

```
top = 0;  bottom = R-1;  left = 0;  right = C-1
result = empty list
while top <= bottom and left <= right
    for j = left to right:          append matrix[top][j]
    top = top + 1
    for i = top to bottom:          append matrix[i][right]
    right = right - 1
    if top <= bottom
        for j = right down to left: append matrix[bottom][j]
        bottom = bottom - 1
    if left <= right
        for i = bottom down to top: append matrix[i][left]
        left = left + 1
print result joined by spaces
```
